correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the stipulated signed-burning update semantics (spread before one manually ignited vertex, no recolouring), a,b>=3, one negative edge u0v0. First ignition spreads to the whole opposite part in the second spreading phase; at most one further opposite-colour ignition is made and by the third spread every remaining vertex has strict majority because each part size >=3. This directly yields green codewords empty, all, each singleton and complement, each of n-2 edges incident to exactly one endpoint of the frustrated edge and complement: size 4n-2 and claimed six-term weight enumerator. Switching is a pointwise sign conjugation of influences, so every signed plurality is n minus Hamming distance to the code. The auxiliary eligible-pair graph is two disjoint stars; its balanced-cut colour-class sizes are 2,a,b,n-2, giving radius floor(n/2)-1 odd or balanced, n/2-2 even unbalanced, with only A/B deepest balanced words. An independently written brute signed-dynamics BFS for (3,3),(3,4),(3,5),(4,4),(4,5),(5,5) reproduced full green codes and covering radii; these are bounded checks, whereas the three-round argument and two-star analysis prove all a,b>=3. K2,3 excluded and known to violate code claim.
